record.title: Argentina requires additional energy and firm power for large AI data-center loads
record.summary: Resolution 264/2026 establishes XDEM rules for large new or expanded loads. XDEM-DATOS requires 80% monthly energy coverage and normally 115% firm-power coverage.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Monthly eligible energy coverage is at least 80%.

brief.importance_rationale: The rule materially changes supply planning for nationally significant AI loads.
limitations: Exporting grid areas may receive a justified firm-power exception.
Eligible supply can include qualifying existing gas-generation expansion.
Registration alone does not authorize operation.
brief.summary: Resolution 264/2026 establishes XDEM rules for large new or expanded loads. XDEM-DATOS requires 80% monthly energy coverage and normally 115% firm-power coverage.

technical.claimed_result: Grid reliability is the stated objective.
technical.demonstrated_result: Published legal requirements; realized compute capacity unmeasured.
technical.mechanism: Contracted eligible additional energy and firm power accompany access review.
technical.novelty: Data loads receive higher firm-power coverage than production loads.
technical.regime: Threshold: 0.5% of reference MEM demand; includes AI training and inference.
technical.reproducibility: Public resolution and annex provide the governing text.
technical.strongest_baseline: General large-user rules are supplemented by XDEM-specific obligations.

brief.why_it_matters: Binding supply obligations can change large AI-campus financing and electricity access.
